title: Cognito Identity Pools
description: Learn how to use Cognito Identity Pools to provide temporary AWS credentials to users and applications.

data.text: **Amazon Cognito Identity Pools** (also called Federated Identities) provide temporary AWS credentials to users so they can access AWS services directly — like uploading a file to S3 without going through your backend server.

An Identity Pool acts as a broker between your users and AWS. When a user authenticates (through a User Pool, Google, Facebook, or another provider), the Identity Pool exchanges those credentials for temporary AWS credentials with limited permissions.

data.title: Core Concepts
items: **Authentication providers** — User Pools, Google, Facebook, Apple, SAML, OIDC
**Temporary credentials** — short-lived AWS access keys (usually 1 hour)
**IAM roles** — policies attached to roles define what the user can access
**Role mapping** — rules that assign different IAM roles based on user attributes
**Guest access** — allow unauthenticated users to get limited access

data.title: Identity Pool with IAM Role Mapping (JSON)
data.content: This example shows how an Identity Pool maps authenticated users to one IAM role and unauthenticated users to another.

data.title: Security Note
data.text: Always follow the principle of least privilege when assigning IAM roles. Never give users more permissions than they need.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Identity Pools give temporary AWS credentials to users
Role mapping lets you assign different permissions to different users
Guest access allows limited functionality for unauthenticated users
